Option D. Marathwada, Khandesh, Vidarbha and Konkan are all sub-regions of one state, Maharashtra. The chapter's own Table 7.1 lists exactly this set, Marathwada, Vidarbha, Khandesh, Konkan and Western Maharashtra, as one group of geographical areas sharing a common factor.

The other three groups each contain one member that does not belong. In A, Satpuda, the Alps and the Rockies are mountain ranges but the Deccan is a plateau. In B, Yavatmal, Amravati and Solapur are districts, and Table 7.1 groups districts together in just that way, but Greater Mumbai is a metropolitan city area rather than a district. In C, the Thar, Sahara and Gobi are deserts but the Himalaya is a mountain range.

Option C. Tropical forest, thorny forest, mangrove forest and deciduous forest are all types of vegetation, which the chapter lists among the natural features that form the basis of a region, alongside physiography, climate, soil and wildlife.

The other three groups each mix categories. In A, plain, mountain and plateau are landforms but a lake is a water body. In B, pressure, temperature and humidity are elements of climate but a river is not. In D, fishing, lumbering and agriculture are primary activities that take produce directly from nature, whereas a bakery processes what has already been produced.
